messages:
maya: heads up — we just saw a burst of fncall rejects from the canary that look like array-vs-object mismatches. Console spammed alerts and the billing tags got noisy. snippet: ```ERROR fncall_validate: expected object, got array: [..] route_id=webhook-v2 policy=strict-canary```

sam: thanks for flagging. is this strictly a schema change in the canary model, or something in the gateway coercion?

maya: looks like the model variant started emitting top-level arrays for attachments when a certain prompt is used. gateway used to coerce, but strict-canary turned off coercion so it now registers as a hard reject.

patrick: ugh. that means two issues: 1) noisy alerts (ops) and 2) misattributed quota/billing because rejects are being counted on the route instead of the canary slice.

lucy: is there an audit id per reject event? iirc we only log reject_reason + route, not which policy caused the reject (canary vs strict).

maya: right now logs have: `reject_reason`, `route_id`, `model_variant`. no policy id. we could add `policy_tag` but need to think about retention/rt cost.

sam: short-term: can we debounce alerting for structured-output rejects? e.g., if >100 rejects for same route+reason in 5m, emit a single high-level alert instead of 100 alerts. reduces pager noise.

patrick: i like debounce. but also we need a way to tie the rejects to rollout changes so SRE can triage. adding an `audit_line` linking to the canary rollout would help. something like `audit_link=rollouts/rl_12345` in the reject event.

lucy: console UX: instead of spamming the notifications pane, show a per-route 'reject heatmap' that surfaces sudden changes and links to the exact policy causing it. clicking opens the auditline with sample payloads (redacted).

ops-bot: deploy: canary strict-validate toggle flipped by @jen at 2025-11-02T14:03:21Z

maya: good — that audit info exists in the rollout meta; we should surface it in the reject event. proposal: add 3 fields to reject telemetry: `policy_id`, `policy_mode` (soft|strict), `audit_ref`. small strings.

sam: agreed. telemetry team: will that blow up our ingest? 3 small strings per reject might be ok if we sample rejects. we already sample 1% of successful responses for evals. maybe for rejects we upsample to 10% but keep the debounce for alerts.

patrick: and for billing attribution — we should ensure rejects from a canary variant are attributed to a special billing key (like `billing_slice=canary`) so cost dashboards don't get confused. then reconcile later if canary is promoted.

lucy: UX also needs a rollback CTA on the heatmap/alert: one-click link that opens the rollout and offers rollback or soft-mode toggle (with confirm). avoids manual hunt.

maya: quick mitigation i pushed: temporarily set strict-canary -> soft for webhook-v2 in eu-west. that will reduce hard rejects while we patch the model.

sam: thanks. follow ups: (1) telemetry change PR to include `audit_ref` + `policy_id` (2) debounce alerting rule in OpsPager (3) console heatmap mock from UX by end of week. anyone want to own the telemetry PR?

patrick: i'll take telemetry PR. will add sampling guard and field schema.

lucy: i'll do the heatmap mock and the rollback CTA flow.

maya: i'll coordinate with model team to get a canary fix and document expected shape.

sam: ops: we'll add a temporary debounce rule: group identical reject_reason+route into 5m bundles and send aggregated alert with count + top sample payload. ops-bot will annotate alert with `audit_ref` when present.

ops-bot: note: created alert-rule #487: "Structured-reject-debounce" (grouping window=5m)

maya: one more thought — add a short example in the console docs showing how to interpret soft vs strict rejects and where billing attribution appears. small docs change can save a lot of slack threads :)

sam: agreed. ok let's track action items in the rollout ticket rl_12345. thanks all :thumbsup:
